ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2023-02-15
Provider: Dr. Lisa Thompson, MD
Department: Obstetrics & Gynecology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Routine prenatal visit at term with discussion of delivery plans given suspected fetal malpresentation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 31-year-old with malignant melanoma, cervical HSIL, and epilepsy returns for prenatal care at term. She reports feeling well with good fetal movement. Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated, and she has received regular prenatal care. The patient expresses a desire for a vaginal delivery if possible.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Malignant melanoma (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion of cervix with unsatisfactory colposcopy (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- Asymptomatic Actinomyces colonization of genital tract (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- Pregnancy (20 weeks gestation) (diagnosed 2022-05-15)
- Anencephaly (diagnosed 2022-08-15)
- False labor (Braxton Hicks contractions) (diagnosed 2022-12-15)
- Epilepsy (generalized seizure disorder, new onset at 12 weeks gestation)
- History of malignant melanoma (back, status post wide local excision)
- History of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL/CIN 2-3) of the cervix

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Wide local excision with 1cm margins, right upper back (melanoma)
- Cervical colposcopy (unsatisfactory visualization)
- Sentinel lymph node biopsy, negative for malignancy

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Carbamazepine 200 mg PO twice daily
- Folic acid 4 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal aunt: Malignant melanoma (age 45)
- Paternal grandmother: Epilepsy
- Mother: Hypothyroidism
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.

VITAL SIGNS:
On examination, her blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 72 bpm, and fetal heart rate is 140 bpm.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
The obstetric examination reveals a fundal height consistent with gestational age, but the fetal position is noted to be breech on Leopold maneuvers.

IMAGING:
An ultrasound confirms a frank breech presentation with no other abnormalities. Amniotic fluid index is normal, and there are no signs of placental insufficiency.
